# Enclosure bounds change

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`counting-under-enclosure` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](counting-under-enclosure.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Enclosure bounds change: from the step it holds, the relata active together with the steps of change stay within the total standing then. Finite and enclosed worlds have the same laws of counting under a selection exactly when it bounds change and binds counting; binding adds at most three more.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Say that B bounds change from step T when at every step t from T on, n t together with the number of steps from T before t at which c or a is positive (occurrences) is at most B. (`Becoming.ChangeBound`, `Becoming.occurrences`)
2. Within a change bound change does not recur; a change bound from step T is one from the first step, larger by T and the counts before T. (`Becoming.ChangeBound.not_recurring`, `Becoming.ChangeBound.from_zero`, `Becoming.changeBound_iff_zero`)
3. Enclosure bounds change: in a world with a census of activity whose relata are all embodied, with a balanced, dissipative flow and every step from T on enclosed, the total standing at T bounds the change of the census from T: across an enclosed step the total standing never rises, and it falls by at least one at every step at which something arises or ceases, while the embodied relata active all stand. (`Becoming.Flow.Enclosed`, `Becoming.World.enclosure_bounds_change`, `Becoming.Flow.standing_never_rises`, `Becoming.Flow.change_lowers`, `Becoming.World.length_le_stock`)
4. Conversely an enclosed queue has natural numbers as members, active and standing at one exactly while in the queue, its front also standing at what the bound leaves beyond one for each member; the front takes part at every step, taking from each member what its standing loses and giving each what it gains. (`Becoming.World.enclosedQueue`)
5. Every step is enclosed by its span, and the queue meets all eight premises under every tally with a change bound from the first step in which nothing joins an empty queue: balance holds by construction, and what stands falls by one at every step of change, so dissipation holds. (`Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_enclosed`, `Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_premised`)
6. So a pointwise property of the counts holds of the census of every world meeting all eight premises with every step from some step on enclosed exactly when it holds of every tally with a change bound from the first step in which nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_counting`)
7. Such a queue never reaches past its B + B * B-th member, and on those places it is a finite world meeting all eight premises, so finite worlds have the same laws of counting, and worlds enclosed from some step on and finite worlds have the same laws of counting. (`Becoming.Queue.reached`, `Becoming.ChangeBound.joins`, `Becoming.ChangeBound.reach`, `Becoming.placesBelow`, `Becoming.World.finiteQueue`, `Becoming.World.finiteQueue_finite`, `Becoming.World.finiteQueue_premised`, `Becoming.World.finite_counting`, `Becoming.World.enclosed_iff_finite_counting`)
8. In the finite queue dissipation binds and the bound is attained: with one member replaced across the first step the front takes two units from the closed family of all places, and what stands at the first step totals two, one member with one step of change behind it making two at every later step. (`Becoming.World.replaced`, `Becoming.World.finite_dissipation_binds`, `Becoming.World.replaced_attains`)
9. That change does not recur cannot be strengthened to an end step: if every tally with a change bound from the first step in which nothing joins an empty queue had a step after which nothing changes, or every finite world meeting the eight premises with decided activity a step after which nothing arises, the limited principle of omniscience LPO would hold, the witness (Swap) replacing one member at the first true of a Boolean sequence. (`Becoming.ChangeBound.lpo_of_ends`, `Becoming.World.lpo_of_finite_ends`, `Becoming.LPO`)
10. Under each selection of the premises: at an enclosed step balance, dissipation and embodiment suffice, for with nothing active the total standing there is nothing and any member coming to stand would lower it, so nothing arises, whoever gives and whoever takes. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_binds_counting`)
11. Whatever its counts, the enclosed queue takes only while active, and it dissipates step by step, asking only that nothing join an empty queue at the step and that both steps stay within what stands. (`Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_taking`, `Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_dissipatesOn`)
12. A queue closing at step T has every relatum exchange a unit each way with the front before T, so no family is closed before T; it balances, from T on its flow is the enclosed queue's and every step is enclosed, and with a change bound from T and nothing joining an empty queue from then on it dissipates. (`Becoming.EnclosedQueue.closing`, `Becoming.World.closingQueue`, `Becoming.World.closingQueue_balanced`, `Becoming.World.closing_flows`, `Becoming.World.closingQueue_enclosed`, `Becoming.World.closingQueue_dissipative`)
13. Say a selection bounds change when it selects balance, embodiment and dissipation. (`Becoming.World.BoundsChange`)
14. So in worlds with every step from some step on enclosed, under each selection of the eight premises a pointwise property of the counts holds of every census of every world meeting the selection exactly when it holds of every tally meeting two conditions: where the selection binds counting, nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active; where it bounds change, from some step T on change stays within a bound and nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_counting_under`)
15. The second condition carries its step: that change does not recur within the bound gives no such step by itself. (`Becoming.ChangeBound.not_recurring`)
16. Without dissipation enclosure leaves counting free: the enclosed queue with bound zero counts every tally meeting the other conditions; without balance or embodiment the still queues are enclosed at every step. (`Becoming.World.still_enclosed`)
17. So under enclosure a change bound from some step, with nothing arising from then on across a step at which nothing is active, is a law of counting under a selection exactly when it bounds change: where it does not, a count growing by one at every step is counted by a world meeting the selection and enclosed from some step on. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_change_bound_iff`)
18. Every step of a finite world is enclosed, so there balance, embodiment and dissipation by themselves bind counting and bound change from the first step, and every census counts at most as many as there are relata. (`Becoming.World.Finite.enclosed`, `Becoming.World.enclosed_binds_counting`, `Becoming.World.enclosure_bounds_change`, `Becoming.World.Finite.census_bounded`)
19. Conversely, seat the members of a queue in turn round a ring of N places (member k + 1 sits at the place after member k's, back at the first place once the ring is full); members less than a full turn apart sit at different places. (`Becoming.Ring.slot`, `Becoming.Ring.slot_add`, `Becoming.Ring.slot_ne`, `Becoming.Ring.slot_inj`)
20. Where at most M are in the queue at each step, a ring of 2M + 1 places holds those in it before or after any step, so the ring lists the places held at each step, each once, and counts what the queue counts. (`Becoming.Ring.size`, `Becoming.Ring.census`, `Becoming.Ring.counts`)
21. A ring with nothing standing meets every premise but embodiment; a ring each of whose places stands at one while held, every premise but balance; and with its front's place also taking from each place what that place's standing loses and giving what it gains, every premise but dissipation, only active relata giving where nothing joins an empty queue. (`Becoming.World.ring`, `Becoming.World.ring_meets`, `Becoming.World.embodiedRing`, `Becoming.World.embodiedRing_meets`, `Becoming.World.balancedRing`, `Becoming.World.balancedRing_acting`, `Becoming.World.balancedRing_meets`)
22. So in finite worlds, under each selection of the eight premises, a pointwise property of the counts holds of every census of every finite world meeting the selection exactly when it holds of every tally meeting three conditions: at most some number active at each step; where the selection binds counting or bounds change, nothing arising across a step at which nothing is active; where it bounds change, change within a bound from the first step. (`Becoming.World.finite_counting_under`)
23. That nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active is a law in finite worlds under a selection exactly when it selects balance and embodiment, and only active relata giving or dissipation; a change bound from the first step is a law exactly where the selection bounds change, one member replaced at every step being counted by a finite ring meeting any other selection; so in finite worlds the 256 selections give three kinds of law. (`Becoming.World.finite_counting_binds_iff`, `Becoming.World.finite_change_bound_iff`)
24. Finite worlds and worlds enclosed from some step on have the same laws of counting under a selection exactly when it bounds change and binds counting: where it does not bound change, a count growing by one at every step is counted by a world enclosed at every step and by no finite world; where it bounds change without binding counting, one relatum arising from none before enclosure is counted by an enclosed world and by no finite world. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_iff_finite_counting_under`, `Becoming.Queue.lone_settles`)
25. With enclosure from some step on, in worlds meeting the eight in which every premise binds, a pointwise property of the counts holds of every census exactly when it holds of every tally with nothing arising across a step at which nothing is active, a change bound from the first step and something arising, the enclosed queue with its web saturated binding every premise, the census included since its relata are the natural numbers. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_binding_counting`, `Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_saturated_binds`)
26. More generally, with enclosure from some step on, under each selection S, a pointwise property of the counts holds of every census of every world meeting S, enclosed from some step on, in which each premise S selects binds exactly when it holds of every tally meeting the two conditions of World.enclosed_counting_under and the three of World.binding_counting_under. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_binding_counting_under`)
27. Enclosure and binding add their laws each on its own, each of the three under exactly the same selections as where nothing is enclosed, since what arises may arise before enclosure. (`Becoming.World.enclosed_binding_activity_iff`, `Becoming.World.enclosed_binding_arising_iff`, `Becoming.World.enclosed_binding_joint_iff`)
28. Witnesses under enclosure: the relay is enclosed at every step and the lossy queue from the step after its gift; without dissipation, a queue whose front exchanges one unit more each way with itself across the step after something joins is enclosed at every step. (`Becoming.World.relayQueue_enclosed`, `Becoming.World.lossyQueue_enclosed`, `Becoming.World.exchangingQueue`, `Becoming.World.exchangingQueue_binding`)
29. With balance, embodiment and dissipation but neither only active relata giving nor only active relata taking, dissipation binds at a closed step only where something stands to be lost, so the queue closes at a step at which something is active, from which on nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active, its front standing one unit more there and shedding it across the step; otherwise the enclosed queue saturated. (`Becoming.Tally.occupied_from`, `Becoming.World.sheddingQueue`, `Becoming.World.sheddingQueue_binding`, `Becoming.World.enclosedQueue_saturated_binds`)
30. No finite world binds the census, so under a selection with the census every property is a law in finite worlds. (`Becoming.World.finite_binding_census`)
31. Under each selection S without it, a pointwise property of the counts holds of every census of every finite world meeting S in which each premise S selects binds exactly when it holds of every tally meeting the three conditions of World.finite_counting_under and three more: something is active where S selects activity needing support, only active relata giving or only active relata taking; something arises where S selects embodiment; and something arises across a step at which something is active where S selects embodiment and bounded transmission with only active relata giving or with both only active relata taking and dissipation. (`Becoming.World.finite_binding_counting_under`)
32. So in finite worlds binding adds exactly that something is active (where activity needing support, only active relata giving, only active relata taking or embodiment is selected), that something arises (where embodiment is), and that something arises across a step at which something is active, exactly where embodiment is selected and the selection binds counting or bounds change, or selects bounded transmission with only active relata giving or with both only active relata taking and dissipation. (`Becoming.World.finite_binding_activity_iff`, `Becoming.World.finite_binding_arising_iff`, `Becoming.World.finite_binding_joint_iff`)
33. This is because every step of a finite world is enclosed: balance, embodiment and dissipation bind counting by themselves, and taking with dissipation gives only active relata giving. (`Becoming.World.Finite.acting`)
34. The finite witnesses are rings with saturated webs: without embodiment, a relay beside a ring handing one of the two units place 1 stands at on to place 0 and losing the other, whatever holds the places. (`Becoming.World.relayRing`, `Becoming.World.relayRing_binding`)
35. With embodiment, without balance and with dissipation or only active relata giving, a lossy ring whose front's place, across one step, exchanges a unit each way with itself and each place coming to be held and loses one unit more. (`Becoming.World.lossyRing`, `Becoming.World.lossyRing_binding`)
36. With embodiment, without dissipation, and without only active relata giving where balance is not selected, a balanced ring whose front's place exchanges one unit more each way with itself across the step after something arises; with balance, embodiment and dissipation, the finite queue with its web saturated (World.finiteQueue_saturated_binds). (`Becoming.World.exchangingRing`, `Becoming.World.exchangingRing_binding`)
37. The exact form for every world of the enclosure bound and of enclosure binding counting is in laws-of-one-step, of which World.enclosure_bounds_change and World.enclosed_binds_counting are corollaries. (`Becoming.World.enclosure_bounds_change`, `Becoming.World.enclosed_binds_counting`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Listing and decidability: as in whole-law-of-counting; read of worlds, decided activity. It is a logical commitment of the representation.
- Pointwise: as in whole-law-of-counting, in place of function extensionality, a hypothesis of the theorems.
- Enclosure and finiteness: every step from some step on enclosed, or the world finite, are conditions on worlds, stated as hypotheses of the theorems, not axioms.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Stated for activity finite at each step.
- It speaks only of the counting of activity; the counts of standing and dependence under the premises are in counting-standing-and-dependence.
- The change bound is the total standing at enclosure, which can be attained but is not the value in every world. Witness: `Becoming.World.replaced_attains`.
- The bound counts steps of change, not events.
- In the enclosed queue activity needing support and bounded transmission hold vacuously (nothing depends on anything); the whole law of counting where every premise binds, adding only that something arises, is in whole-law-of-counting.
- No finite world binds every premise; the laws in finite worlds where every premise but the census binds are in whole-law-of-counting.
- Change does not recur, and an end step needs omniscience in general. Witness: `Becoming.ChangeBound.lpo_of_ends`.
- **Counterexample:** Swap with ChangeBound.lpo_of_ends: replacing one member at the first true of a Boolean sequence has its change bounded by two and change does not recur there, while an end step constructed for every such count is LPO. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Population.lean)
- **Counterexample:** World.replaced_attains: the bound is attained, so enclosure_bounds_change cannot be strengthened; World.lpo_of_finite_ends: in finite worlds meeting the eight premises a step after which nothing arises needs omniscience in general. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Counting.lean)
- **Counterexample:** World.closingQueue and World.enclosed_counting_under: with balance, embodiment and dissipation selected but neither only active relata giving nor taking, arising before enclosure is unconstrained, members joining an empty queue before step T in the queue closing at T; without dissipation, the enclosed queue with bound zero counts every tally, and enclosure adds no law. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Counting.lean)
- **Counterexample:** World.finite_change_bound_iff and World.enclosed_iff_finite_counting_under: one member replaced at every step is counted by finite rings meeting every premise but embodiment, balance or dissipation, so a change bound is a law of finite worlds only where the selection bounds change; a count growing by one at every step is counted by queues enclosed at every step, and in Queue.lone_settles one relatum arises from none before enclosure, so under the other selections finite and enclosed worlds have different laws of counting. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Counting.lean)
- **Counterexample:** World.finite_binding_joint_iff and World.finite_binding_census: with embodiment selected but a selection neither binding counting nor bounding change, nor selecting bounded transmission with only active relata giving or with only active relata taking and dissipation, one relatum arising from none across the first step and staying (Queue.lone) is counted by a finite world meeting the selection in which each selected premise binds, nothing being active at the step it arises; so the third law is a law only under the selections named. In finite worlds it holds under more selections than where nothing is enclosed (whole-law-of-counting): with embodiment, balance and dissipation but neither only active relata giving nor taking, and with embodiment, only active relata taking, dissipation and bounded transmission but neither balance nor only active relata giving. With the census selected no finite world binds the selected premises, and every property is vacuously a law. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Counting.lean)
- **Counterexample:** World.enclosed_binding_joint_iff: with embodiment, balance and dissipation selected but a selection neither binding counting nor selecting only active relata giving and bounded transmission, the same relatum arising from none and staying (Queue.lone) is counted by a world enclosed from the first step on, meeting the selection, in which each selected premise binds (a shedding queue, whose front sheds its spare unit across the first step), nothing being active at the step it arises: in finite worlds the third law holds here, under enclosure from some step on it does not, since what arises may arise before enclosure. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Counting.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · Uses decidability of the named determinations, a logical commitment written as a hypothesis. · Properties of counts respect values step by step (pointwise), in place of function extensionality. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

The rest theorem (ceasing-needs-arising, continued-change-needs-openness) says change does not recur under enclosure; this result gives its quantitative form and all it says of counting: in an enclosed unfolding the counts are constrained by a change bound and by nothing more than the tally and the eight premises (whole-law-of-counting); under all eight premises, in counting, finite worlds cannot be told from worlds enclosed from some step on, and under a selection of the premises they cannot be told apart exactly where it bounds change and binds counting; what enclosure adds appears exactly where balance, embodiment and dissipation are selected, and finiteness adds a bound on the count and the constraint of dissipation on arising from the first step. The author's reading (an AI argument): the change bound is what the stepwise dissipation of the total standing under enclosure looks like in the counts; in an enclosed unfolding every forming or dissolving spends something standing in the relations, and what can change without end is the open unfolding (continued-change-needs-openness); without dissipation a closed family can be given to without taking, and enclosure no longer constrains counting; a finite world is enclosed from the first step, so there only active relata taking is not needed: dissipation with balance and embodiment already makes arising need what is present. This is the counting of activity, whose English names arising and ceasing Ren confirmed (2026-10-09-arising-ceasing-names; the Chinese 生起／止息 being the AI's rendering); it is not the proposal's generative and degenerative (Ren wrote ‘generative和degenerate虽然都在一个becoming model上，但是他们不overlap吧’, a tag question presuming that they do not overlap, so this reading is not what is meant; they read as widening and narrowing what can form, DELEGATED-CHOICES D2); it evaluates neither arising, ceasing nor rest.

**Law family:** The census and the laws of counting (lead: [census-balance](census-balance.md)). What comes to be and what ceases are counted against one list: the list at the end with what ceased is the list at the start with what came. The members state that balance and its halves (ceasing needs arising; under a continuation, a bounded census and enclosure), where the counts exist (where what they count is decided), the census read off the exchange, and what the premises add to the tally. ### History

- 2026-10-10: added as P35 of the unification plan, following Ren's ‘aim a complete theory of becoming, and finish related work’; answers whole-law-of-counting's next step, the laws of counting in finite worlds and under enclosure; the drafts were checked by the thirteenth independent review and rebuilt following its U4–U6 (the law stated once, with a change bound from the first step; the realizing worlds without a start step or ground relata; an end step implying LPO); the names follow Ren's naming criteria of 10 October, the drafts' ‘budget’ becoming the change bound; see §48 and §49 of the integration note.
- 2026-10-10 P38: following Ren's ‘go ahead with Part I’, the claim adds the laws of counting under each selection of the premises with enclosure: at an enclosed step balance, dissipation and embodiment suffice (World.enclosed_binds_counting), the queue closing at step T (World.closingQueue) and the full characterization (World.enclosed_counting_under); the enclosed queue takes only while active whatever its counts and dissipates step by step (World.enclosedQueue_taking, World.enclosedQueue_dissipatesOn). Title, correspondence, counterexamples, limitations and next step updated. The claim under all eight premises is unchanged. The author's counterreview is in §52 of the integration note.
- 2026-10-10 P38b: completing in finite worlds what each premise adds in Part I (Ren: ‘the strongest claim without axiom, as the first part’), the claim adds the laws of counting under each selection in finite worlds: the witnesses are rings seating the members of a queue in turn (Ring, World.ring, World.embodiedRing, World.balancedRing), the characterization is World.finite_counting_under, with two exact conditions (World.finite_counting_binds_iff, World.finite_change_bound_iff), and finite and enclosed worlds have the same laws of counting exactly where the selection bounds change and binds counting (World.enclosed_iff_finite_counting_under). Title, correspondence, counterexamples, limitations and next step updated; the correspondence's earlier ‘in counting, finite worlds cannot be told from enclosed ones’ is now restricted to all eight premises. The author's counterreview is in §54 of the integration note.
- 2026-10-13 takeover reconciliation: current consolidated receipt 20261013T094743.528770Z contains 22 inherited modules; the carried-over count of 15 in the current validation summary is corrected to 22. Historical receipts and their original counts remain unchanged, as do the claim, premises and proofs.
- 14 October 2026, general laws and renames (plan section 10, study section 112): the study only adds section 112 (general laws and renames) and its paragraph in the English summary; the unification plan only adds the 14 October 2026 rename table after the P36 table in section 10; chapter: §9 gains rows for Stock, LossMatching and Contacts, rewrites six rows (Capture, TimedResponse, Revision, ReferencePlan, ContinuingRevision, RepairComparison) and drops the P83 label of the Identification row; the consolidated totals follow receipt 20261013T204910.042715Z (4861 theorems, 6856 declaration audits, 86 closure modules) and the complete-episode paragraph cites that receipt; renamed Lean names in the text and glossary take their new names, and the former wording becomes “the learner given the bound” and “perturbing the state alone”. This record's claim, premises and status are unchanged; no reproof is credited.

The naming sentence's list of names and its gloss of Ren's criteria stand behind the names-provisional key and remain in the snapshot; the review's findings were U4–U6, and the four sections of the author's counterreview are §49, §52, §54 and §63 of the integration note. In the counterexamples ‘than in P45’ became ‘than where nothing is enclosed (whole-law-of-counting)’. The local restatement appended to the next step became law 37.
